The GAO noted that staffing shortages have created 'significant blind spots' in oversight, particularly regarding hazardous material routes.

Rail industry representatives counter that real-time data sharing between companies has created a 'force multiplier' effect that compensates for reduced federal presence. 'We have a financial incentive to keep tracks safe,' said Association of American Railroads spokesperson Linda Park. 'Every incident costs millions in liability and downtime.'

Congressional critics argue that the current framework relies too heavily on corporate goodwill. 'We're essentially asking foxes to guard henhouses,' said Senator Mark Stevens (D-OH), who plans to introduce legislation restoring pre-2018 inspection standards. The bill faces strong opposition from industry lobbyists who maintain that increased regulation would divert resources from actual safety improvements to compliance paperwork.
